text: Beeton’s 1861 British household manual recommends recording every payment in a daily diary, however small. At month’s end, the household rearranges those entries under trades such as butcher and baker, turning scattered purchases into comparable spending categories (§16).

text: In Beeton’s 1861 household system, accounts are balanced at least monthly against the cash actually remaining. The diary is not merely a memory aid: its total must agree with money in hand, and one month’s expenditure can be compared with another (§16).

text: Beeton advises a housekeeper to record supplies delivered on credit before their bills arrive. The delivery book can then be compared with tradesmen’s invoices, exposing discrepancies and providing a measure of normal household consumption (§56, Britain, 1861).

text: Beeton’s 1861 British manual says an employer should explain every expected duty when engaging a domestic servant. The instruction treats an incomplete description of the job as a cause of later disputes; it is advice for households employing servants (§17).

text: Beeton recommends speaking to a domestic servant’s former employer rather than relying solely on an unfamiliar written reference. The applicant first arranges a convenient appointment, so the inquiry follows the etiquette of a planned visit (§18, Britain, 1861).

text: For a dinner served à la russe, Beeton recommends laying a menu beside each guest and arranging flowers and some dessert dishes along the middle of the table. The printed bill of fare lets diners anticipate a sequence served from elsewhere (Britain, 1861).

text: For a large tea party, Beeton recommends two teapots instead of crowding a single pot with leaves. When more tea is needed, she calls for emptying the spent leaves and making a fresh infusion (recipe 1814, British household manual, 1861).

text: Beeton’s café noir is strong, sweetened after-dinner coffee served in very small cups without milk or cream; brandy or liqueur is optional. The recipe locates the drink within a particular meal ritual in her 1861 British household manual (1813).
